newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stock index plunges, more downside seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stock index plunges, more downside seen.

text.p: Singapore stocks headed south with the key Straits Times Industrials Index ending 21.29 points down at 1,993.49, dragged down by food company Cerebos Pacific.
The last time the STI index ended below 2,000 was on April 29, 1997 when it closed at 1,990.20.

Index-linked Cerebos hit a 42-month low of S$6.45 as analysts downgraded the stock after its disappointing first half earnings and warnings of a tougher second-half. It rebounded slightly to end at S$6.75 (US$4.75), down S$1.25 on over 2.6 million shares traded.
Market turnover was a moderate 104.99 million shares, with 109 gainers to 224 losers.
Debutante Huan Hsin, which makes telephone cords, ended at US$0.465 against its initial public offer of US$0.42. Volume was over 12.4 million shares.

Dealers said soft drink company Fraser & Neave Ltd was hurt by Cerebos's poor results and sold ahead of its half-year results on Friday. Analysts are expecting it to post a 20 percent decline in profits. The stock ended S$0.20 cents down at S$10.50.
Multimedia Creative Technology fell S$1.50 to S$22.70 after a failed lawsuit against Cyrix Corp for infringing on its copyright.
